title: A Cartier divisor gives a supported Kummer map
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an arbitrary integer $m\geq1$. Put $A=A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, and let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. The coefficient sheaf $A_T$ and the finite-level Tate twist $A_T(1)$ are those of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] on the small pro-etale site; in particular this notation is not redefined by an etale tensor product. Let $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ be an effective Cartier divisor, a closed subscheme whose ideal is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor, and put $L=\mathcal O_T(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. There is a canonical morphism in the ordinary pro-etale derived category [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]
$$c_{D,A}:i_*A_D\longrightarrow A_T(1)[2].$$
Its composite with $A_T\to i_*A_D$ is $c_{1,A}(L)$. Here $c_{1,A}$ is the etale Kummer boundary at any exponent $\ell^r$ killing $A$, extended to $A$ and pulled to the pro-etale site using [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], followed by the canonical projection-induced identification with the specified Tate twist. This definition is independent of $r$. For any morphism $h:T'\to T$ for which $D'=D\times_TT'$ is again Cartier, under the canonical supported-constant and Tate-twist comparisons, $h^{-1}c_{D,A}=c_{D',A}$. The construction is compatible with coefficient reductions $A_{E,b}\to A_{E,a}$ for $b\geq a\geq1$. No divisibility of $m$ by the ramification index is assumed. The etale-origin witness for the target is $\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A$; the same supported morphism on this etale witness gives the ordinary etale formulation used by etale callers.

proof.text: Choose $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$ (one may take $r=m$: $\ell$ has positive integral valuation in $\mathcal O_E$, hence $\ell^m\in(\varpi_E^m)$). For steps 1-6 put $n=\ell^r$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$ and $B_{r,T}=\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes^L_\Lambda A$; these are auxiliary etale objects, not a definition of $A(1)$. The dual ideal $L$ of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] has a canonical section $s_D$, dual to $\mathcal I_D\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_T$. On an open chart where $\mathcal I_D=(f_a)$ with $f_a$ a nonzerodivisor, the ideal is free on $f_a$, its dual is free on $e_a=f_a^{-1}$, and $s_D=f_ae_a$. On $V=T-D$, $f_a$ is a unit, so $s_D$ is a nowhere zero section and gives a specified trivialization $\tau_D:\mathcal O_V\cong L|_V$. On overlaps $e_b=(f_a/f_b)e_a$, hence these formulas agree. The frame torsor $P_D=\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}(\mathcal O_T,L)$ of [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor] is therefore a $\mathbf G_m$-torsor with the specified section $\tau_D$ on $V$.

source.place: Proof, etale finite-torsion auxiliary construction, before comparison with the chapter twist

proof.text: Apply [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] to $(P_D,\tau_D)$ with $G=\mathbf G_m$. This gives a specified class $\alpha_D\in H^1(T,V;\mathbf G_m)$, independent of chart equations and refinements, whose forgotten-support image is the torsor class of $L$. For explicit changes of equations, $f'_a=u_af_a$ gives $e'_a=u_a^{-1}e_a$ and $f'_ae'_a=f_ae_a$; it is the same line bundle with the same section, not just an unspecified lift of its Picard class. The relative lemma supplies the comparison with derived sections; no assertion that an arbitrary ordinary Cech cover computes all derived cohomology is needed.

source.place: Proof, etale finite-torsion auxiliary construction, before comparison with the chapter twist

proof.text: Since $n$ is invertible on $T$, [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] supplies the short exact Kummer sequence $0\to\mu_n\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{n}\mathbf G_m\to0$. Apply its relative connecting map, provided by [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology], to $\alpha_D$: $\beta_D=\delta_{T,V}(\alpha_D)\in H^2(T,V;\mu_n)$. The relative lemma's compatibility with forgetting support gives $\operatorname{forget}(\beta_D)=\delta_T([L])$, exactly $c_{1,\Lambda}(L)$. Only the abelian-sheaf Kummer sequence is used: $\mathbf G_m$ is not a $\Lambda$-module and is never tensored over $\Lambda$.

source.place: Proof, etale finite-torsion auxiliary construction, before comparison with the chapter twist

proof.text: Use the canonical comparisons from module-derived sections to abelian-derived sections for the sheaf $\mu_n$ on $T$ and its restriction on $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget] they induce isomorphisms on every cohomology group, hence are quasi-isomorphisms. They commute with restriction because both restriction maps send a section to its restriction. Taking their cones therefore identifies $H^2(T,V;\mu_n)$ with the relative cohomology computed in $\Lambda$-module sheaves; the projection from the shifted cone to the $T$-sections complex also commutes with these comparisons. Taking degree two in [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], with coefficient ring $\Lambda$ and $K=\mu_n[0]$, identifies it with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)}(i_*\Lambda_D,\mu_{n,T}[2])$. Define $c_{D,\Lambda}$ to be the morphism corresponding to $\beta_D$. The forget-support map is precomposition with $\Lambda_T\to i_*\Lambda_D$: applying derived Hom to this map is the first arrow into the ordinary sections complex in the support cone. Thus step 3 is precisely the required first Chern class assertion. This is a support-Hom identification and uses no purity isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, etale finite-torsion auxiliary construction, before comparison with the chapter twist

proof.text: Apply the exact derived change-of-rings functor of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] along $\Lambda_T\to A_T$ to $c_{D,\Lambda}$. Its target is $B_{r,T}[2]$ by the stated definition. Its source is canonically $i_*A_D$. Indeed, [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] gives the stalk of $i_*\Lambda_D$ as $\Lambda[0]$ on $D$ and zero off $D$. The derived monoidal inverse-image comparison [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], the stalk-as-pullback identification [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback], and the constant-sheaf pullback [lem-kun-pullback-constant] therefore compute the stalks of $(i_*\Lambda_D)\otimes^L_\Lambda A$ as respectively $\Lambda\otimes^L_\Lambda A=A[0]$ and zero. The canonical change-of-coefficients comparison to $i_*A_D$ is the identity at these stalks. Exact stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and conservative geometric stalks [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] show it is an isomorphism of derived objects (apply them to every cohomology sheaf of its cone). Apply the same functor to the equality of step 4; the restriction map becomes $A_T\to i_*A_D$ by the identical stalk calculation. Its composite is $c_{1,A}(L)$ by definition. This constructs $c_{D,A}$ without any flatness assumption on $A$.

source.place: Proof, etale finite-torsion auxiliary construction, before comparison with the chapter twist

proof.text: Let $h:T'\to T$ and assume $D'$ is Cartier. Pull the above charts back: $f'_a=h^*f_a$ generates the pulled-back ideal and is a nonzerodivisor by this assumption, so $e'_a=(f'_a)^{-1}$ is its dual basis. The transition equality $e'_b=h^*(f_a/f_b)e'_a$ and section equality $s_{D'}=f'_ae'_a$ identify $(h^*L,h^*s_D)$ with $(\mathcal O_{T'}(D'),s_{D'})$. This computation requires no flatness of $h$. Pullback of the frame torsor is taken with the coefficient map $h^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,T}\to\mathbf G_{m,T'}$, not an assumed isomorphism of those two sheaves. Naturality of the relative torsor class and of its connecting maps in [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] now sends $\alpha_D$ and $\beta_D$ to $\alpha_{D'}$ and $\beta_{D'}$: the maps of Kummer sequences send $u$ to its pulled-back unit and satisfy $h^*(u^n)=h^*(u)^n$. The map $h^{-1}\mu_{n,T}\to\mu_{n,T'}$ is an isomorphism: at every geometric point it is the identity map on the $n$ distinct roots of $X^n-1$ over an algebraically closed field; invertibility of $n$ makes these roots etale locally lift, exactly as in the root-cover argument giving [lem-amb-kummer-any-base]. Apply the natural support-Hom identification [lem-amb-closed-support-hom]; its source comparison $h^{-1}i_*\Lambda_D\to i'_*\Lambda_{D'}$ is the identity $\Lambda\to\Lambda$ on the pulled-back support and $0\to0$ elsewhere by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] and [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback], so is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] applies these comparisons to complexes and their cohomology sheaves. Finally [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] and [lem-kun-pullback-constant] identify the pullback of derived extension to $A$ with derived extension after pullback. All these comparison maps are the indicated unit or tensor maps, so their naturality applies to the morphism, giving $h^{-1}c_{D,A}=c_{D',A}$, including equality after forgetting support.

source.place: Proof, etale finite-torsion auxiliary construction, before comparison with the chapter twist

proof.text: By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] (1), $\mu_{\ell^r}$ is locally free of rank one over $\Lambda$; thus $B_{r,T}$ is the ordinary tensor in degree zero, even if $A$ is not flat over $\Lambda$. Write $M=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_T$. Clause (2) identifies the projection reduction $M\otimes_{\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,T}}\Lambda_T$ with $\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{proet}}$. Clauses (3)-(4) identify $\mathcal O_E(1)\otimes_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}}A_T$ with the original $A_T(1)$ in degree zero for every $m$. Apply clause (3) also at index $er$, where $e$ is the ramification index: $(\varpi_E^{er})=(\ell^r)$, since the two generators differ by a unit. It identifies $\mathcal O_E(1)/\ell^r$ with $M\otimes_{\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,T}}(\mathcal O_E/\ell^r)_T$. Tensor this equality along $(\mathcal O_E/\ell^r)_T\to A_T$; associativity gives the projection-induced isomorphism $A_T(1)\cong\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{proet}}\otimes_{\Lambda_T}A_T$. This uses reduction of the completed line, not an assertion that $A$ is free over $\Lambda$. More explicitly, the original definition gives $A_T(1)=M\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T}A_T$ by tensor associativity. Since $\ell^rA=0$, this is $(M/\ell^rM)\otimes_{\Lambda_T}A_T$. The quotient $M/\ell^rM$ is also $M\otimes_{\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,T}}\Lambda_T$: both are the cokernel of multiplication by $\ell^r$ on $M$. Thus the reduction of clause (2) applies to the original constant-ring tensor, and the comparison sends $x\otimes a$ to $p_r(x)\otimes a$, where $p_r:M\to\mu_{\ell^r}$ is the inverse-limit projection. This formula specifies the map used below and all its coefficient comparisons. The canonical map $\nu_T^*\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\to\mu_{\ell^r,T}^{\mathrm{proet}}$ comes from pulling units. On the etale root-trivializing cover of clause (1) it sends a chosen primitive root generator to the same root generator and is the identity between constant rank-one $\Lambda$-modules; it is therefore an isomorphism. [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] identifies pulled constant coefficients and preserves the exact functor on complexes. Tensor comparison here is underived: the tensor is the cokernel of the bilinearity relations in the free module, and this exact inverse image preserves that presentation. Consequently there is a specified isomorphism $q_{r,T}:\nu_T^*B_{r,T}\cong A_T(1)$, inverse to the projection map just constructed.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: identification of the extended Kummer coefficient with the chapter Tate twist and transport of the morphism

proof.text:
Let $j:T-D\hookrightarrow T$. This open immersion is quasi-compact: on an affine chart on which the Cartier ideal is generated by $f$, the complement is the quasi-compact principal open $D(f)$; quasi-compactness is local on the target. Apply [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement] to the etale constant $A_T$ and apply the exact functor [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. By [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] its first arrow becomes $j_!A_{T-D}	o A_T$ on the pro-etale site. By [lem-sf-proetale-open-closed-sequence], its cokernel is $i_*A_D$, and the quotient map is the adjunction unit. Thus the canonical comparison $a_T:
u_T^*(i_*^{\mathrm{et}}A_D)\cong i_*^{\mathrm{proet}}A_D$ is the unique quotient isomorphism identifying these two maps out of $A_T$. If $\widetilde c_{D,r,A}$ denotes the etale morphism of steps 1-6, define
$$c_{D,A}=q_{r,T}[2]\circ
u_T^*(\widetilde c_{D,r,A})\circ a_T^{-1}.$$
Precomposition with the supported restriction is then $q_{r,T}[2]
u_T^*(c_{1,r,A}(L))$, precisely the specified $c_{1,A}(L)$. No full-faithfulness assertion has been used as a twist comparison.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: identification of the extended Kummer coefficient with the chapter Tate twist and transport of the morphism

proof.text: For $s\geq r$, the diagram of Kummer sequences with exponent $\ell^s$ on top and $\ell^r$ below has middle map $u\mapsto u^{\ell^{s-r}}$, right map the identity and kernel map $\mu_{\ell^s}\to\mu_{\ell^r}$ given by that same power. Therefore naturality of the relative boundary in [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology] sends $\beta_{D,s}$ to $\beta_{D,r}$. After extension to $A$, its kernel map is an isomorphism: locally compatible primitive roots identify it with the identity $A\to A$. The projections of $M$ satisfy $p_r=p_{s,r}p_s$ by the inverse-limit definition [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], so $q_{r,T}$ and $q_{s,T}$ commute with this comparison. The displayed formula for $c_{D,A}$ is consequently independent of $r$; two unrelated allowed choices are compared through their maximum. For reductions $A_{E,b}\to A_{E,a}$ choose one $r$ killing both. The tensor maps send $x\otimes b$ to $x\otimes\bar b$, and the projection formulas for both $q$ maps are identical on these tensors; extension of the supported constant source sends $1\otimes b$ to $\bar b$. Thus extension of $c_{D,A_{E,b}}$ is $c_{D,A_{E,a}}$, and for three indices the quotient composites agree. For a Cartier-preserving $h$, step 6 gives the equality on the etale witnesses. The site comparisons commute with $h$ because both inclusions act identically on underlying schemes and base change; uniqueness of left adjoints gives the composition comparison. The maps $a_T$ commute with it since both are the quotient by the same open extension-by-zero map. The maps $q_{r,T}$ commute with it: for local units $h^*(u^{\ell^{s-r}})=h^*(u)^{\ell^{s-r}}$, so all finite-root projections and the tensor maps $x\otimes a\mapsto h^*x\otimes a$ commute. On the root-trivializing covers they identify the finite twists with the identity map of the constant $A$-line. Substitute these equalities and the step-6 equality into the formula of step 8 to obtain $h^{-1}c_{D,A}=c_{D',A}$. The quotient, projection and tensor maps are identity maps for identity pullback and compose for two pullbacks, proving coherence as well as the equality after forgetting support.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ be an effective Cartier divisor.
There is a natural morphism in the ordinary derived category

$$
c_D:i_*A_D\longrightarrow A_T(1)[2].
$$

Its image after forgetting support is
$c_1(\mathcal O_T(D))$. For any base change under which
the pullback divisor remains Cartier, the map pulls back to
the corresponding map for that divisor.

proof.text:
First take coefficients $\mathbf Z/n$. Write
$v:T-D\hookrightarrow T$. The line bundle
$\mathcal O_T(D)$, together with its canonical trivialization
on $T-D$, defines an element of

$$
H^1\bigl(\operatorname{Cone}(R\Gamma(T,\mathbf G_m)
\longrightarrow R\Gamma(T-D,\mathbf G_m))[-1]\bigr).
$$

For completeness, choose local equations $f_a$ of $D$.
The transition units $f_a/f_b$ define the line bundle,
and the invertible functions $f_a$ on the complement give
its specified trivialization. The equality
$(f_a/f_b)(f_b/f_c)=f_a/f_c$ is the cocycle equation,
and restriction of the transition units is the coboundary of
these trivializing functions. These two assertions are exactly
the cocycle equation in the displayed relative cone. Replacing
$f_a$ by a unit times $f_a$ changes that cocycle by a
coboundary. Refining the covering preserves its class. One may
compute the cone on an injective resolution, or on etale
hypercovers refining this covering; the description gives the
same class in either computation.

Apply the connecting map of the Kummer sequence
[lem-amb-kummer-any-base] to this relative class. It gives
$c_D\in H_D^2(T,\mu_n)$. Forgetting the relative
trivialization sends it to the Kummer boundary of the line
bundle, namely its first Chern class. The support triangle in
[lem-amb-closed-support-hom] identifies

$$
H_D^2(T,\mu_n)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T,\mathbf Z/n)}
(i_*\mathbf Z/n,\mu_n[2]).
$$

This identification uses the sheaf-level adjunction between
$i_*$ and sections supported on $D$, derived by
injective resolutions; it does not assert a purity isomorphism.
All the cone maps and Kummer boundaries commute with pullback
of the pair and its trivialized line bundle. This proves the
asserted base-change compatibility whenever the pulled-back
pair is again the Cartier pair of
[def-sc-effective-cartier-divisor].
Finally apply derived scalar extension from $\mathbf Z/n$
to $A$. Its source is $i_*A_D$, as seen on stalks,
and its target is $A_T(1)[2]$ by
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. No flatness of $A$ over
$\mathbf Z/n$ is needed.
